science.title: Why colostrum is special
science.text: Colostrum is the very first milk a mother produces — a dense package of immunoglobulins (antibodies), growth factors, lactoferrin and proteins designed to kick-start a newborn's immune system and gut. In powder form you get a bigger daily dose than a capsule: 2,300 mg standardized to 25% IgG, to support your immune defences, the lining of your gut, and a healthy inflammatory response.

format.title: A bigger dose, mixes clean
format.text: Powder lets you take a full 2,300 mg of colostrum in one scoop — far more than a capsule. It's unflavoured, so stir it into water, milk or a smoothie without changing the taste.
list: — 1 scoop (2.3 g) = 2,300 mg colostrum (575 mg IgG)

items.a: Colostrum is the first milk a mother produces after birth — extra-rich in antibodies (immunoglobulins), growth factors and proteins that support immunity and gut health. Ours is bovine colostrum standardized to 25% IgG.

items.q: Powder or capsules — what's the difference?
items.a: Same colostrum, bigger dose. One scoop of powder gives 2,300 mg (575 mg IgG), versus 500 mg in a capsule — handy if you want a higher daily amount and don't mind mixing a drink.
No — colostrum is a dairy product, so it contains milk and isn't suitable for vegans or those with a milk allergy.
Ideally on an empty stomach, such as first thing in the morning, so the bioactive proteins absorb well. Take it daily for best results.
Anyone with a milk allergy, and those pregnant or nursing, under 18, immunocompromised, or with a medical condition should consult a physician before use.
